Fix `plugins/techdocs/src/reader/components/TechDocsReaderPage/useFormerRefRedirect.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. SECURITY — HIGH. The live-entity gate is dead code in production, so a hostile descriptor claiming a LIVE entity's ref captures that entity's docs traffic, and the resolution query fires on EVERY docs page view instead of only after a miss (violating the hot-path promise for the docs route).

The hook signature is `useFormerRefRedirect(entityRef: CompoundEntityRef, entity?: Entity)` and its ONLY live-holder guard is `if (entity) { return undefined; }` at line 55. But the single production call site, TechDocsReaderPage.tsx:205, calls `useFormerRefRedirect(memoizedEntityRef)` with ONE argument. So `entity` is permanently undefined there and the guard never fires. `resolveFormerEntityRef` performs no live-holder check of its own either — its own TSDoc states it 'must be called only after a direct lookup for the requested ref has already missed'.

FIX IT STRUCTURALLY, so no caller can omit the check. Do NOT keep relying on the caller passing an argument, and do NOT make the parameter merely required — the entity is not in scope at the call site (line 91 is inside a documentation comment and line 249 is a render-prop callback that runs AFTER this hook). Instead make the hook fetch the entity itself and gate on the result, exactly as its sibling `useExternalRedirect` in the same directory already does (it is in your context files): that hook calls `await catalogApi.getEntityByRef(entityRef)` inside its own `useAsync` and decides from the result.

Concretely, inside the existing `useAsync` body and BEFORE any call to `resolveFormerEntityRef`:
  1. `const existing = await catalogApi.getEntityByRef(entityRef)` (wrapped so a throw is swallowed, as this is a render path that must not throw — the existing try/catch and the sibling's pattern both show this).
  2. If `existing` is truthy, `return undefined` — a live entity holds the requested ref, so it wins unconditionally and NO resolution query may be issued.
  3. Only when the direct lookup missed, call `resolveFormerEntityRef(catalogApi, entityKey)` as it does today.

Remove the now-redundant `entity?: Entity` parameter and its `if (entity)` guard, and drop the `Entity` import if it becomes unused. Update the TSDoc `@param` list to match the new signature, and keep the `@internal` tag. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the `checkedEntityRef` remount guard, the `entityKey` dependency, the sub-path/query/fragment preservation, the `{ replace: true }` navigation with `state: { formerEntityRef }`, and the `shouldShowProgress` computation. Keep the Apache 2.0 header with year 2026 unchanged.

The caller TechDocsReaderPage.tsx:205 already passes exactly one argument, so it keeps compiling unchanged.

Fix `plugins/techdocs/src/reader/components/TechDocsReaderPage/useFormerRefRedirect.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:

The hook under test is being changed to fetch the entity itself and gate on the result (see its new implementation in your context files): it now calls `catalogApi.getEntityByRef(entityRef)` first, returns early when a live entity holds the requested ref, and only calls `resolveFormerEntityRef` when that direct lookup missed. The `entity?: Entity` second parameter is REMOVED.

Update this test file to the new contract, and ADD the security regression test that proves the live-entity gate:

  - NEW TEST (this is the important one): when a LIVE entity holds the requested ref — i.e. `getEntityByRef` resolves to an entity — assert BOTH that `mockNavigate` was NOT called AND that `resolveFormerEntityRef` was NOT called. The second assertion is as important as the first: it proves no resolution query is issued on the hot path for a ref that resolves normally.
  - Update the existing cases to drive behaviour through the `getEntityByRef` mock instead of a second hook argument: the redirect case mocks `getEntityByRef` to resolve undefined (a miss) and `resolveFormerEntityRef` to resolve `{ status: 'resolved', entity, formerEntityRef }`; the 'does nothing when the entity exists' case mocks `getEntityByRef` to resolve an entity.
  - Keep the 'checks once per entity and survives a failing lookup' intention: make the lookup reject and assert it is attempted at most once per entity ref (the checkedEntityRef guard) and that no navigation happens.

Call the hook with ONE argument everywhere — passing a second argument will no longer typecheck.

Keep repo conventions: fewer-but-thorough multi-assertion tests, `screen` and `findBy*` over waitFor for DOM queries, no test IDs added to implementations, and the Apache 2.0 header with year 2026 unchanged. Return the WHOLE file.

ADD a test case asserting the newly closed oracle, and keep every existing test in this file byte-identical:
